I am a healthcare executive, educator, and health economist with 20 years of senior leadership experience in Canadian public-sector health organizations. I use quantitative modelling to examine health system resilience, access, and value, and educate health leaders to support informed, evidence-based decision-making.

Health systems frequently discuss access; however, they typically measure utilization. The gap between the two is where systems fail people, and it is where my work is focused.

::: {.pillar}
### Leadership
Senior leadership roles across hospitals, health authorities, and research institutes, encompassing capital programs valued at up to CAD \$100 million, the development of new health facilities, and governance in the not-for-profit sector.
:::

::: {.pillar}
### Research
Health system resilience to climate shocks in Western Province, Zambia, and the economics of the HPTN 071 (PopART) trial with Imperial College London. [More on my research →](research.qmd)
:::

::: {.pillar}
### Teaching
Adjunct Professor at the Schulich School of Business, where I designed and teach Value and Quality in Healthcare (MHIA 6160), and Sessional Lecturer in the Master of Public Health program at the University of Waterloo. [More on my teaching →](teaching.qmd)
:::

I am seeking leadership opportunities in applied research, innovation, and education across public agencies, health systems, research institutes, universities, and colleges. The best way to reach me is by [email](mailto:cbchiarot@uwaterloo.ca?subject=Connecting%20via%20your%20website) or [LinkedIn](https://www.linkedin.com/in/cameronchiarot).
